name: BTC Monday effect (long Mondays only)
author: Guglielmo Maria Caporale, Alex Plastun
summary: Bitcoin returns on Mondays are significantly higher than on other weekdays; a trading simulation that buys at the start of Monday and sells at its end is profitable, though mostly not significantly different from random.
notes: Signal at Sunday close so the Monday (dow 0) bar is held; flat the rest of the week. Sample 2013-2017. Also summarized at quantpedia.com/the-day-of-the-week-effect-in-the-crypto-currency-market/ and CESifo WP 6716.

name: Hold BTC only on Mondays and Saturdays
author: Santiment
summary: Monday (+0.69%) and Saturday (+0.5%) were the best average days; holding only on those days from 2018 gained ~68% while buy-and-hold lost ~38%, but the edge vanished when the start was moved to 2017.
notes: Signal on Friday close holds Saturday; signal on Sunday close holds Monday. Author warns the late-2018 crash fell on a Monday; start-date sensitive.

name: BTC end-of-month effect with 22-day trend filter
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Bitcoin has a tailwind over the last days of the month and first days of the next; 109 trades averaged +3.3% (67% winners, CAGR ~42% with 16% exposure), and requiring close above the close 22 days ago improved results.
notes: Exact optimized entry/exit days are behind a bot wall/paywall ('a few days before month end, exit a few days into the new month'); param grid spans the plausible window. The unfiltered stock version is already in practitioner (pr-turn-of-month).

name: Turn-of-month (-1,+3) for BTC and ETH
author: Evangelos Vasileiou
summary: Optimized four-day windows show the most profitable periods straddle month end; the classic last-day-plus-first-three-days window is among them and gives better risk-adjusted (not always absolute) returns than buy-and-hold in BTC and ETH.
notes: Signal at close of the second-to-last day so the last day and days 1-3 are held. Kumar (2022, Managerial Finance) reports the same TOM window significant for BTC/ETH/LTC 2015-2021.

name: Buy BTC every October 1st, sell September 30th
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: Buying at the October 1 open and selling the next September 30 had only two losing years since 2011 (average +203%, worst -55%), with halving-year entries strongest.
notes: Effectively buy-and-hold with a one-day annual exit; included as a published calendar rule. Halving-year subset (2012/2016/2020) cannot be expressed exactly without a year variable.

name: Buy BTC November 1st, sell January 1st
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: Holding BTC from the November 1 open to the January 1 open averaged +40% (+23% ex-2013 outlier), with all halving-year instances positive, though the author says the history is too short for significance.
notes: Halving-year-only variant not expressible without a year variable (could approximate with days_since_halving < 250).

name: Uptober: hold BTC during October only
author: The Rogue Quant
summary: October was Bitcoin's best month over the last decade (~+21% average, positive 9 of 10 years); hold BTC only through October.
notes: Author flags small sample and that significance tests are paywalled. Same 'Uptober' claim widely repeated (tastycrypto, Livewire, Decrypt).

name: Hold BTC except in September
author: Decrypt
summary: September is Bitcoin's worst month on average over the last decade (average around -5%); sit out September and hold the rest of the year.
notes: No published backtest of the avoid rule; the source reports the monthly averages. Flat from Sep 1 to Sep 30 (re-enter on Sep 30 close).

name: Short BTC in September
author: ETF Trends
summary: Because of the recurring September weakness in Bitcoin, a bearish (inverse) crypto ETF could benefit during September.
notes: Source frames it as buying an inverse BTC ETF for September; no formal backtest.

name: Halloween effect (long November-April)
author: Southeast Asian Journal of Economics (five-cryptocurrency calendar study)
summary: Tests the equity Halloween effect (returns higher November-April than May-October) on five major cryptocurrencies 2010-2020; rule = hold only November through April.
notes: Evidence for crypto is weak/mixed; other studies (Ozcan et al. 2024) find no Halloween effect. Rule taken from the standard definition the paper tests.

name: Reverse January effect (short BTC in January)
author: Ozcan, Khan, Iftikhar
summary: EGARCH tests on BTC, ETH, XRP, USDT, USDC find no Halloween effect; the only month-level return pattern is a reverse (negative) January effect.
notes: Paper is a statistical test, not a trading system; rule is the direct translation (short through January).

name: April effect in Bitcoin (long April)
author: Ozcan, Khan, Iftikhar
summary: Month-of-year dummies show April significant for Bitcoin (February for Ethereum); hold BTC only in April.
notes: Direct translation of a significant month dummy; sign assumed positive per the summary. ETH-February variant would be a separate test.

name: February effect in Ethereum (long February)
author: Ozcan, Khan, Iftikhar
summary: February is the statistically significant month for Ethereum returns; hold ETH only in February.
notes: Direct translation of a significant month dummy; sign assumed positive.

name: BTC 4 down closes below 50MA but above 100MA, hold 7 days
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: After 4 straight lower closes with BTC below its 50-day but above its 100-day MA, buying the next open and holding 7 days won 62% of 21 trades since 2011 (avg +7.8%, PF 4.66).
long_entry: (close < shift(close, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(close, 2)) & (shift(close, 2) < shift(close, 3)) & (shift(close, 3) < shift(close, 4)) & (close < sma(close, 50)) & (close > sma(close, 100))
long_exit: highest((close < shift(close, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(close, 2)) & (shift(close, 2) < shift(close, 3)) & (shift(close, 3) < shift(close, 4)) & (close < sma(close, 50)) & (close > sma(close, 100)), n) < 1
notes: Fixed hold encoded as 'exit when no signal in the last n bars' (re-signals extend the hold; the original skipped overlapping signals). 60-day hold reported avg win +129%.

name: BTC 8 straight down closes, hold 7 days
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: Buying after 8 consecutive lower daily closes and holding 7/15/30 days lost every time since 2011 (avg -9.3% at 7 days); long streaks signal continued weakness, not a bounce.
short_entry: (close < shift(close, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(close, 2)) & (shift(close, 2) < shift(close, 3)) & (shift(close, 3) < shift(close, 4)) & (shift(close, 4) < shift(close, 5)) & (shift(close, 5) < shift(close, 6)) & (shift(close, 6) < shift(close, 7)) & (shift(close, 7) < shift(close, 8))
short_exit: highest((close < shift(close, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(close, 2)) & (shift(close, 2) < shift(close, 3)) & (shift(close, 3) < shift(close, 4)) & (shift(close, 4) < shift(close, 5)) & (shift(close, 5) < shift(close, 6)) & (shift(close, 6) < shift(close, 7)) & (shift(close, 7) < shift(close, 8)), n) < 1
notes: Source tested the LONG side and found 0% winners on a tiny sample (4 occurrences at 1-day spacing); encoded as the short implied by the finding. Very rare signal.

name: BTC 60-day closing low above 200MA, hold 90 days
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: A 60-day closing low while above the 200-day MA, held 90 days, had PF ~21 since 2011 (9 trades) but negative expectancy in the last 5 years.
notes: Author highlights regime dependence: recent 5 years poor. Fixed hold encoded via highest(signal, n).

name: BTC 5-day closing low above a rising 50MA, hold 30 days
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: Buying a 5-day closing low while above a rising 50-day MA and holding 30 days won 59.5% of 79 trades since 2011 (avg +14.2%, PF 3.62); 7-day hold had no edge.
notes: 'Rising' taken as 50MA above its value one day earlier (source does not define the slope window).

name: BTC 40-day low above 100/200/365MA, hold 90 days
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: A close at a 40-day low while above the 100, 200 and 365-day MAs, held 90 days, averaged +13.5% since 2016 excluding early outliers, with a recent cluster of gains.
long_exit: highest((close <= lowest(close, 40, 1)) & (close > sma(close, 100)) & (close > sma(close, 200)) & (close > sma(close, 365)), n) < 1
notes: Trade count and win rate not given in text.

name: BTC 4 straight up weeks, hold 8 weeks
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: After four consecutive higher weekly closes, buying the next weekly open and holding 8 weeks won 78.6% of 28 trades since 2011 (avg +70%, +59.5% ex-2013).
long_exit: highest((dow == 6) & (close > shift(close, 7)) & (shift(close, 7) > shift(close, 14)) & (shift(close, 14) > shift(close, 21)) & (shift(close, 21) > shift(close, 28)), n) < 1
notes: Weekly bars emulated with Sunday (dow 6) closes 7 days apart; 8-week hold = 56 days.

name: BTC weekly bearish engulfing, buy and hold 2 weeks
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: A weekly bearish engulfing candle in BTC is less bearish than believed: 40 cases, 2-week forward average -3.5% (PF 0.55), but with weekly RSI(3) >= 90 the prior week it turned positive (10 cases, 60% win, +5.7%).
notes: Weekly candles emulated from daily bars ending Sunday (week open = open 6 days ago). Base result was negative after the pattern, so encoded as a 2-week short; the weekly-RSI(3) bullish refinement needs weekly RSI and is not expressed.

name: Bitcoin halving cycle strategy (buy N days before, sell N days after halving)
author: Gabremoku
summary: Pure calendar model: buy a fixed number of days before each halving and sell a fixed number of days after it, without any price indicator.
notes: Script defaults not visible; params are illustrative. Days to the next halving approximated as cyc - days_since_halving (actual epochs ran ~1320-1440 days).

name: Halving clock: hold from cycle bottom to ~535 days after halving
author: Quantpedia
summary: Cycle tops fell 525-546 days after each halving and bottoms ~365-406 days after tops, timing that survives null tests where price indicators decay; implies holding from the bottom window until ~535 days post-halving.
notes: Article gives timing observations, not explicit rules; rule derived from stated top (525-546d) and bottom (~top+365-406d) windows. Only three cycles.

name: Halving event drift (day -15 to +10)
author: Quantpedia
summary: Around halvings BTC drifts slightly lower from day -50 to -15, then appreciates until about day +10; suggests a 'buy the rumor, sell the news' swing long.
notes: Only three halvings; days to next halving approximated with cyc. Author calls it speculative.

name: Long BTC on CME futures expiration Friday
author: Quantpedia
summary: Over 2017-2024 BTC gained significantly on CME expiration day (last Friday of the month) after a negative day before; pattern reversed after the BITO launch in late 2021.
notes: Signal at the Thursday close before the last Friday; holds the expiry Friday. Article gives charts, not explicit rules; regime flipped post-BITO.

name: Long BTC the Monday after CME expiration
author: Quantpedia
summary: The first Monday after the last-Friday CME expiration was the best day by return in the 2017-2024 sample.
notes: Sunday two days after the last Friday has days_to_month_end <= 4 or falls on dom 1-2 of the next month.

name: BTC pre-holiday drift (D-1 to D+1 around US holidays)
author: Quantpedia
summary: Buying BTC (BITO) the day before US holidays and selling at the close of D+1 is mostly flat on its own (base), the setup for the attention-filtered version.
notes: Only fixed-date US holidays expressible (New Year, Juneteenth, July 4, Veterans Day, Christmas); floating holidays (MLK, Presidents, Memorial, Labor, Thanksgiving) omitted. Calendar days used since BTC trades daily.

name: BTC pre-holiday drift with N-day-high attention filter
author: Quantpedia
summary: Within D-5..D+5 of US holidays, buy BTC only when it closes above its prior N-day high (N=5/10/20) and hold one day; significantly positive average returns, Sharpe > 0.6.
notes: Fixed-date US holidays only (see base entry); +-5 calendar-day windows. 5-day version best but most volatile.

name: BTC 21:00-23:00 UTC intraday seasonality
author: Quantpedia (Padysak, Vojtko)
summary: Buying BTC at 21:00 UTC and selling at 23:00 UTC returned ~33% annualized with -22% max drawdown 2015-2022; strongest on Fridays.
notes: Needs hourly bars; daily vocabulary cannot express an intraday window. Also quantpedia.com/strategies/intraday-seasonality-in-bitcoin.

name: BTC 21-23 UTC seasonality only in high-volatility regimes
author: Quantpedia
summary: Restricting the 21:00-23:00 UTC trade to days when 30-day volatility exceeds its 365-day median raised Calmar to ~1.96 (37% annualized, -19% max DD) on 2015-2023 Gemini data.
notes: Intraday hourly window; not expressible on daily bars.

name: BTC at 10-day high, overnight on Fri/Mon/Tue only
author: Quantpedia
summary: Most returns of the MAX(10) rule come from NYSE-overnight sessions; final proposal buys at the NYSE close when BTC is at a 10-day high only on Friday, Monday and Tuesday nights (35%+ OOS, ~-12% DD for base).
notes: Rough daily approximation: original enters at 16:00 New York and exits next morning (Friday trade spans the weekend). Daily version holds the next full UTC day.

name: Bitcoin CME weekend gap fill
author: TradingView community
summary: Gaps between the CME Bitcoin futures Friday close and Sunday open are claimed to fill (at least ~65%) eventually; trade toward the gap.
notes: Needs CME futures session prices; spot BTC trades 24/7 and has no gap.

name: Hammer in downtrend (close below 20MA), hold 5 days
author: The Rogue Quant
summary: Textbook hammer after a close below the 20-day MA, buy next bar and hold 5 bars: PF 1.30, 61% winners over 44 trades on ES futures 2007-2025.
long_entry: ((min(open, close) - low) >= 2 * abs(close - open)) & ((high - max(open, close)) <= 0.1 * (high - low)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(sma(close, 20), 1))
long_exit: highest(((min(open, close) - low) >= 2 * abs(close - open)) & ((high - max(open, close)) <= 0.1 * (high - low)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(sma(close, 20), 1)), 5) < 1
notes: Hammer geometry from Investopedia definition quoted by the author (lower wick >= 2x body, small upper shadow); exact code paywalled. Original market: S&P E-mini.

name: Any hammer, hold 5 days
author: The Rogue Quant
summary: Dropping the downtrend requirement and trading every hammer improved results (120 trades, PF 1.62, 63% winners on ES 2007-2025).
long_entry: ((min(open, close) - low) >= 2 * abs(close - open)) & ((high - max(open, close)) <= 0.1 * (high - low))
long_exit: highest(((min(open, close) - low) >= 2 * abs(close - open)) & ((high - max(open, close)) <= 0.1 * (high - low)), 5) < 1
notes: The third ('avoid obvious hammers') filter is paywalled and not expressed.

name: Hammer candle, buy next open, exit 10 days later
author: Barry D. Moore (Liberated Stock Trader)
summary: 2,219 hammer trades on Dow stocks over 20 years (TrendSpider detection), entered at next open and exited 10 days later: 52.1% accuracy and only +0.18% per trade.
long_entry: ((min(open, close) - low) >= 2 * abs(close - open)) & ((high - max(open, close)) <= 0.1 * (high - low))
long_exit: highest(((min(open, close) - low) >= 2 * abs(close - open)) & ((high - max(open, close)) <= 0.1 * (high - low)), 10) < 1
notes: Negative-ish evidence (near-zero edge). Hammer geometry approximated; TrendSpider's exact detector not published.

name: Bullish engulfing, buy next open, exit 10 days later
author: Barry D. Moore (Liberated Stock Trader)
summary: 3,735 bullish engulfing trades on 30 Dow stocks over 20 years, entered next open and exited 10 days later, to measure the pattern's real success rate.
notes: On 24/7 crypto the open equals the prior close, so engulfing reduces to an up day whose close exceeds the prior day's open.

name: Inverted hammer, buy next open, exit 10 days later
author: Barry D. Moore (Liberated Stock Trader)
summary: Tests whether the inverted hammer bullish-reversal candle is worth trading, using the same next-open entry and 10-day exit method.
long_entry: ((high - max(open, close)) >= 2 * abs(close - open)) & ((min(open, close) - low) <= 0.1 * (high - low))
long_exit: highest(((high - max(open, close)) >= 2 * abs(close - open)) & ((min(open, close) - low) <= 0.1 * (high - low)), 10) < 1
notes: Exit method assumed identical to the site's other candle studies (next open, 10 days); geometry approximated.

name: Three white soldiers / three black crows with 200 EMA filter
author: Backtrex
summary: Long on three white soldiers above EMA(200), short on three black crows below it, 1:2 stop/target; on USD/JPY 1h 2016-2026 it lost 68.6% (PF 0.75, 30% win rate).
long_entry: (close > open) & (shift(close, 1) > shift(open, 1)) & (shift(close, 2) > shift(open, 2)) & (close > shift(close, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) > shift(close, 2)) & (close > ema(close, 200))
short_entry: (close < open) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(open, 1)) & (shift(close, 2) < shift(open, 2)) & (close < shift(close, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(close, 2)) & (close < ema(close, 200))
notes: Original 30/60-pip stop/target on hourly FX rescaled to 4%/8% for daily BTC (keeps the 1:2 ratio); EMA-cross exit added as a fallback. Published result strongly negative.

name: BTC 20-day low then up close above 200MA, hold 30 days
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: When BTC trades at a >=20-day low but closes up on the day while above its 200-day MA, a 30-day hold averaged +26% with a 74% hit rate (early outlier excluded).
notes: 'Trades at a 20-day low' taken as the intraday low at/below the prior 20-day low; trade count not stated.

name: End of a 30+ day streak below the 200SMA, hold months
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: After BTC's streaks of 30+ consecutive closes below the 200-day SMA ended, returns 6-12 months later were positive in 9 of 11 cases (avg +77% at 6 months for the 3 longest).
notes: Event = first close back above the 200SMA after >=30 closes below (source references the last day below; entry timing unspecified). Tiny sample (11 streaks).

name: Halving 'Quarter Point' long
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: Every point one quarter of the way between halvings (2013, 2017, 2021) was followed by new all-time highs; buy at the quarter point of the cycle.
notes: No entry/exit defined in the article (qualitative, 3 events). Quarter point ~ cycle/4 ~ 350-360 days; exit window is our assumption (n_end).

name: Inside bar momentum (Babypips)
author: Babypips (ported on QuantConnect forum)
summary: Bullish mother bar followed by an inside bar: buy stop 10% of the mother range above its high, stop 20% of range below the high, target 80% of range above; shorts mirror. Forum porter could not make it profitable.
long_exit: highest((shift(close, 2) > shift(open, 2)) & (shift(high, 1) < shift(high, 2)) & (shift(low, 1) > shift(low, 2)) & (close > shift(high, 2) + 0.1 * (shift(high, 2) - shift(low, 2))), n) < 1
short_exit: highest((shift(close, 2) < shift(open, 2)) & (shift(high, 1) < shift(high, 2)) & (shift(low, 1) > shift(low, 2)) & (close < shift(low, 2) - 0.1 * (shift(high, 2) - shift(low, 2))), n) < 1
notes: Stop-order breakout approximated by a close beyond the trigger the day after the inside bar. Range-based stop/target (20%/80% of mother range) cannot be expressed relative to entry; replaced by an n-day time exit.

name: Inside bar with 50 EMA trend filter (Trade Pro claim, myth-busted)
author: myncrypto (testing a Trade Pro strategy)
summary: Bullish inside bar closing above the 50 EMA, enter on a break of the inside bar high, stop at the EMA, target 1.5R (shorts mirror); claimed 75% win rate, but the tester could not reproduce it after costs.
notes: Original on 4h bars with staggered targets; daily version uses the EMA stop as exit and a fixed 6% target as a proxy for 1.5R.

name: Inside bar breakout with 200 EMA market filter
author: StrategyQuant
summary: Stop orders outside the mother bar catch the breakout from an inside-bar consolidation, with a trailing stop and a 200-EMA market filter that sharply cuts drawdowns.
notes: Article gives no exact parameters (full config in a video). Filter applied to the traded asset instead of SPY; trailing stop approximated by an n-day-low exit.

name: Outside bar reversal
author: StockSharp
summary: Bullish outside bar after a bearish bar = long, bearish outside bar after a bullish bar = short; exit on a close beyond the outside bar's extreme; vendor claims ~121% annual return, best in crypto.
notes: Default is 5-minute bars with a 1% stop; daily version here. 'Close below the outside bar low' approximated by a close below the lowest low of the prior n bars.

name: Bearish engulfing traded LONG, exit close above prior high
author: TradesViz
summary: Buying (not selling) a high-volume bearish engulfing candle and exiting on a close above the prior bar's high won 75.8% of 33 ES trades; 'every trading book has it backwards'.
notes: Original on 15-minute ES; 'above-average volume' taken as above the 20-bar average.

name: Bearish engulfing long, conservative (volume 1.5x, RSI < 40)
author: TradesViz
summary: Conservative contrarian variant: bearish engulfing with volume >= 1.5x average and RSI below 40, bought long; 61.9% winners over 21 trades, +6.1%.
notes: Exit for this variant not stated; same close-above-prior-high exit as the base test assumed.

name: Three white soldiers with RSI(14) < 35
author: TradesViz
summary: Three consecutive bullish candles while RSI(14) is still below 35 (oversold) won 83% of 36 ES trades.
notes: Exit not stated; close-above-prior-high assumed. Signal likely rare on daily BTC.

name: Hanging man traded long after a 5-bar rise
author: TradesViz
summary: Hanging-man context (higher high and higher low than 5 bars ago, prior 5-bar gain > 2%, low volume) bought long on AAPL: 64% winners but +4.3% vs +24% buy-and-hold.
long_entry: (high > shift(high, 5)) & (low > shift(low, 5)) & (roc(close, 5) > 2) & (volume < sma(volume, 20)) & ((min(open, close) - low) >= 2 * abs(close - open))
notes: roc assumed in percent. Exit not stated; close-above-prior-high assumed. Hanging-man shape approximated by lower wick >= 2x body.

name: Morning star with SMA(24) and rising-ATR filter
author: TradesViz
summary: Three-candle morning star with price above its 24-bar SMA and ATR above its 10-bar average: 52% winners, -2.4% on AAPL (pattern failed).
long_entry: (shift(close, 2) < shift(open, 2)) & (abs(shift(close, 1) - shift(open, 1)) < 0.3 * abs(shift(close, 2) - shift(open, 2))) & (close > open) & (close > (shift(open, 2) + shift(close, 2)) / 2) & (close > sma(close, 24)) & (atr(14) > sma(atr(14), 10))
notes: Morning-star geometry approximated (small middle body < 30% of first body, third closes above first-body midpoint); exit not stated.

name: Simple doji long
author: TradesViz
summary: Buying a doji (open and close nearly equal) won 66% of 97 AAPL trades for +1.6%.
notes: Doji threshold (body <= 10% of range) assumed; exit not stated.

name: BTC BRD higher-low market-structure reversal
author: neverstop_dd
summary: Long after a pivot higher low followed by a confirmed break above the last swing high (short mirrors with lower high / break of swing low), with ATR or percent stop and RR-based target.
long_entry: (lowest(low, n) > lowest(low, n, n)) & (close > highest(high, n, 1))
short_entry: (highest(high, n) < highest(high, n, n)) & (close < lowest(low, n, 1))
notes: Pivot detection not in vocabulary; higher low approximated as the last n-bar low above the previous n-bar low. Defaults not published; stop/target illustrative at 1:2.

name: Hammer long with volume oscillator and DMI filters
author: Skyrexio
summary: Hammer (lower shadow >= 2x body) long entries filtered by a volume oscillator and DMI values; author backtest on RENUSDT claims 90% winners, PF 7.4.
notes: Invite-only script; filter thresholds, exits and risk settings not disclosed (30-60 minute charts).

name: Bearish engulfing / three outside down / bullish harami long, exit close above prior high
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Buying SPY whenever a bearish engulfing, three outside down or bullish harami appears and exiting when the close exceeds yesterday's high: 474 daily trades, 73% winners, +0.43% avg, PF 2.1 (daily beat weekly).
long_entry: ((shift(close, 1) > shift(open, 1)) & (close < open) & (close <= shift(open, 1))) | ((shift(close, 2) > shift(open, 2)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(open, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) <= shift(open, 2)) & (close < shift(close, 1))) | ((shift(close, 1) < shift(open, 1)) & (close > open) & (close < shift(open, 1)) & (open >= shift(close, 1)))
notes: Pattern definitions not given in the article; standard textbook geometry used. On 24/7 crypto open == prior close, so harami uses open >= prior close.

name: Bearish engulfing bought long, fixed hold (QS rank #1)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Ranked best of 75 candlestick patterns on the S&P 500 as a BUY signal: ~+0.46% average after 5 days, more than double the normal 5-day return.
notes: Fixed 1-20 day holds tested in source; 5-day highlighted.

name: Three outside down bought long, 3-day hold (QS rank #2)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: The bearish three-outside-down reversal works as a short-term mean-reversion buy: ~+0.58% average after 3 days on the S&P 500.
long_exit: highest((shift(close, 2) > shift(open, 2)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(open, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) <= shift(open, 2)) & (close < shift(close, 1)), n) < 1
notes: Definition: up candle, bearish engulfing of it, then a lower close.

name: Dark cloud cover bought long (QS rank #3)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Dark cloud cover (strong up candle then a candle opening higher and closing below its midpoint) performed consistently as a buy signal across holding periods on the S&P 500.
long_exit: highest((shift(close, 1) > shift(open, 1)) & (open >= shift(close, 1)) & (close < (shift(open, 1) + shift(close, 1)) / 2) & (close > shift(open, 1)), n) < 1
notes: Gap-up open is not possible on 24/7 data (open == prior close), so the open condition degenerates to equality.

name: Bullish piercing line, long hold (QS rank #4)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Piercing line (down candle followed by an up candle closing above its midpoint) is weak short term but matches the market drift on longer holds.
long_exit: highest((shift(close, 1) < shift(open, 1)) & (close > open) & (close > (shift(open, 1) + shift(close, 1)) / 2) & (close < shift(open, 1)), n) < 1
notes: Gap-down open condition dropped (no gaps in 24/7 data).

name: Three inside up, 10-20 day hold (QS rank #5)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Three inside up (bullish harami followed by a breakout close) beat average when held more than 10 days; 20-day return about twice normal, but rare.
long_exit: highest((shift(close, 2) < shift(open, 2)) & (shift(close, 1) > shift(open, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(open, 2)) & (close > shift(open, 2)), n) < 1
notes: Standard definition: down candle, small up candle inside its body, third candle closes above the first candle's open.

name: Bullish harami, short hold (QS rank #6)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Most frequent of the top-10 patterns; a slight edge in the first few days after the signal that fades with longer holds.
long_exit: highest((shift(close, 1) < shift(open, 1)) & (close > open) & (close < shift(open, 1)) & (open >= shift(close, 1)), n) < 1
notes: open >= prior close because 24/7 crypto opens at the prior close.

name: Neutral doji, fixed hold (QS rank #7)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Neutral doji buy signals returned roughly in line with the market's upward bias; occurs fairly often.
notes: Doji threshold (body <= 5% of range) assumed; differs from cal-doji-long-tradesviz by threshold and time exit.

name: Long-legged doji, fixed hold (QS rank #8)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Long-legged doji (tiny body, long upper and lower shadows) appears rarely and gives modest positive returns as a buy signal.
long_entry: (abs(close - open) <= 0.1 * (high - low)) & ((high - max(open, close)) >= 0.3 * (high - low)) & ((min(open, close) - low) >= 0.3 * (high - low))
long_exit: highest((abs(close - open) <= 0.1 * (high - low)) & ((high - max(open, close)) >= 0.3 * (high - low)) & ((min(open, close) - low) >= 0.3 * (high - low)), n) < 1
notes: Shadow thresholds assumed.

name: Bullish marubozu, longer hold (QS rank #9)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: A long up candle with almost no shadows is slightly negative over the next few days but positive on longer holds.
long_exit: highest((close > open) & ((close - open) >= 0.95 * (high - low)) & ((high - low) > atr(14)), n) < 1
notes: 'Long' candle taken as range above ATR(14); shadow tolerance 5% assumed.

name: Bearish separating lines bought long (QS rank #10)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Strong up candle followed by a down candle opening at the prior candle's open: ~+0.36% after 10 days over 63 S&P 500 trades.
notes: Requires an opening gap back to the prior open; on 24/7 crypto the open equals the prior close, so the pattern cannot form.

name: QS combined top-5 candlestick patterns, exit close above prior high
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Combining the five best-ranked patterns as SPY buy signals with a close-above-yesterday's-high exit: 515 trades, 74% winners, PF 2.4, 8.3% CAGR, 13% max DD, ~20% exposure.
long_entry: ((shift(close, 1) > shift(open, 1)) & (close < open) & (close <= shift(open, 1))) | ((shift(close, 2) > shift(open, 2)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(open, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) <= shift(open, 2)) & (close < shift(close, 1))) | ((shift(close, 1) > shift(open, 1)) & (close < (shift(open, 1) + shift(close, 1)) / 2) & (close > shift(open, 1))) | ((shift(close, 1) < shift(open, 1)) & (close > open) & (close > (shift(open, 1) + shift(close, 1)) / 2) & (close < shift(open, 1))) | ((shift(close, 2) < shift(open, 2)) & (shift(close, 1) > shift(open, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(open, 2)) & (close > shift(open, 2)))
notes: Article does not name the five; assumed ranks 1-5 (bearish engulfing, three outside down, dark cloud cover, piercing line, three inside up).

name: Outside day, hold next day
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Tests the day after an outside bar (four up/down configurations); on SPY the average next-day gain is zero, below a random day's 0.04%, and other ETFs look random too.
notes: Bearish-close outside day chosen as the mean-reversion configuration; source reports no edge (negative-control strategy).

name: Options-expiration week long (third-Friday week)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Buying the S&P 500 at the open of options-expiration week and selling at the close of expiration Friday: +0.2% per week, 2% CAGR with ~18% exposure since 1993; strongest in April, weakening recently.
notes: Third Friday = Friday with dom 15-21; signal on the preceding Sunday close holds Monday-Friday. Equity OPEX calendar applied to BTC as an approximation of expiry flows.

name: Options-expiration Friday only
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Holding SPY only on monthly expiration Friday (buy the Thursday close) compounded to -23.6% with 51% winners; a 50-day MA filter did not fix it.
notes: Negative published result; included as a test case.

name: Friday the 13th long
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Buying the S&P 500 at the close on Thursday the 12th and selling Friday the 13th: 114 trades, +0.11% avg vs 0.04% random, 54% winners, PF 1.3, mostly due to March 2020.
notes: Very rare signal (1-3 per year).

name: Last day of the month (negative seasonality)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Buying SPY at the close of the second-to-last trading day and selling at the last day's close averaged -0.05% (CAGR -0.7%) since 1993: the last trading day is one of the weakest of the month.
notes: Source tested the long side and found it negative; encoded as the implied one-day short. Calendar month end used (BTC trades every day).

name: Santa Claus rally (last 5 days of December + first 2 of January)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Stocks tend to rise in the last five trading days of the year and the first two of the new year (Hirsch's Santa Claus rally); buy before the window and sell after it.
notes: Paywalled; window taken from the standard Stock Trader's Almanac definition in the article title. Calendar days used for BTC.

name: First day of the month long
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: The first trading day of the month is historically one of the strongest days for stocks; buy at the prior month's last close and sell at the first day's close.
notes: Paywalled; rule follows the article title. Calendar first day for BTC.

name: Turnaround Tuesday (buy a down Monday)
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: When Monday closes lower than the prior close, buy at Monday's close and sell at Tuesday's close; markets tend to reverse on Tuesday after a weak Monday.
notes: Rules paywalled; base version from the free summary (Monday down vs Friday close). For BTC the prior close is Sunday's, not Friday's.

name: Three down days, hold one day
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: After three consecutive lower closes, buying at the close and selling the next morning captured most of the S&P 500/Nasdaq rebound edge.
notes: Original exits at the next open (overnight only); daily bars force a full next-day hold. Re-signals extend the hold while the streak continues.

name: Three lower highs and lower lows, exit close above prior high
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Buy after three consecutive days of lower highs and lower lows and sell when the close exceeds yesterday's high; a short-term mean-reversion edge in stock indices.
long_entry: (high < shift(high, 1)) & (low < shift(low, 1)) & (shift(high, 1) < shift(high, 2)) & (shift(low, 1) < shift(low, 2)) & (shift(high, 2) < shift(high, 3)) & (shift(low, 2) < shift(low, 3))
notes: Rules paywalled; 3-day count and exit follow QS's standard version of this setup. Different from Connors 3-Day High/Low (no MA filters).

name: NR7 narrow-range day, buy and exit close above prior high
author: QuantifiedStrategies (after Toby Crabel)
summary: When today's range is the narrowest of the last 7 days (Crabel's NR7), buy at the close and sell on the first close above yesterday's high; QS reports an improved version beats the raw pattern.
notes: Enhancements are paywalled; base NR7 with QS's usual exit.

name: 4-year presidential election cycle
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Stock returns vary over the 4-year US presidential cycle, with pre-election years strongest and midterm years weakest.
notes: Needs a calendar-year variable; vocabulary only has month/dom/dow (days_since_halving is a different 4-year clock).

name: Pre-Easter rally
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Tests whether stocks rally in the days before the Easter holiday.
notes: Easter is a moving date that cannot be derived from month/dom/dow.

name: ETH 60-day closing low above 200MA, hold 60-90 days
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: ETH closing at a 60-day low while above its 200-day MA: short holds (7-30d) were poor but 60-90 day holds were positive on average (+1.1% to +9.3%) since 2016; 180 days leaned bearish.
notes: Results reported jointly for three query variants; per-query tables are images.

name: ETH 60-day closing low with rising 200MA, hold 60-90 days
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: Variant: ETH 60-day closing low while the 200-day MA is rising (price may be below it); intermediate-term (60-90 day) average trades positive.
notes: 'Rising' taken as above its value one day earlier.

name: ETH 60-day closing low with RSI(14) <= 40, hold 60-90 days
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: Variant: ETH 60-day closing low with RSI(14) at or below 40; positive average trades at 60 and 90 days, weak at 7-30 days.

name: ETH 4 up closes at a 365-day high, <20% above 20MA, hold 90 days
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: When ETH closes higher 4 days straight at a 365-day high without being stretched (>20%) above its 20-day MA, a 90-day hold won all 5 historical trades (avg +102.6%).
long_entry: (close > shift(close, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) > shift(close, 2)) & (shift(close, 2) > shift(close, 3)) & (shift(close, 3) > shift(close, 4)) & (close >= highest(close, 365)) & (close < 1.2 * sma(close, 20))
long_exit: highest((close > shift(close, 1)) & (shift(close, 1) > shift(close, 2)) & (shift(close, 2) > shift(close, 3)) & (shift(close, 3) > shift(close, 4)) & (close >= highest(close, 365)) & (close < 1.2 * sma(close, 20)), n) < 1
notes: Only 5 trades; author warns not significant.

name: ETH/BTC monthly +30% controlling candle
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: Monthly ETH/BTC candles gaining 30%+ at the start of an upswing have never had their low (or open) broken; those levels act as support.
notes: Observation only: no entry, exit or hold given, and 'start of an upswing' is discretionary. Could be built from eth_close/btc_close but there is no rule to encode.

name: Weekly hammer at a rising MA after a 3-week pullback
author: Options Trading IQ
summary: A completed weekly hammer (lower wick >= 2x body) at the bottom of a 3-candle pullback touching a rising 20/50/200-period MA, confirmed Monday above Friday's high; sold as bull put spreads, 87% winners over 30 trades (~10 days each).
long_entry: (dow == 6) & ((min(close, shift(open, 6)) - lowest(low, 7)) >= 2 * abs(close - shift(open, 6))) & ((highest(high, 7) - max(close, shift(open, 6))) < (min(close, shift(open, 6)) - lowest(low, 7))) & (shift(close, 7) < shift(close, 14)) & (shift(close, 14) < shift(close, 21)) & (lowest(low, 7) < lowest(low, 7, 7)) & (lowest(low, 7) <= sma(close, n)) & (sma(close, n) > shift(sma(close, n), 7))
long_exit: highest((dow == 6) & ((min(close, shift(open, 6)) - lowest(low, 7)) >= 2 * abs(close - shift(open, 6))) & ((highest(high, 7) - max(close, shift(open, 6))) < (min(close, shift(open, 6)) - lowest(low, 7))) & (shift(close, 7) < shift(close, 14)) & (shift(close, 14) < shift(close, 21)) & (lowest(low, 7) < lowest(low, 7, 7)) & (lowest(low, 7) <= sma(close, n)) & (sma(close, n) > shift(sma(close, n), 7)), 10) < 1
notes: Weekly candles emulated from Sunday-ending 7-day windows; 20/50-week MAs as 140/350-day SMAs. Original trades a put credit spread with Monday confirmation; approximated as a 10-day long in the underlying.

name: Green hammer near the previous day's low, hold 5 days
author: The Rogue Quant
summary: Coded hammer (green, tiny upper wick < 0.2x body, long lower wick) bought next day and held 5 days on ES; restricting to hammers near the prior day's low was NOT profitable and underperformed the baseline.
long_entry: (close > open) & ((high - close) < 0.2 * (close - open)) & ((open - low) >= 2 * (close - open)) & (abs(low - shift(low, 1)) <= 0.005 * close)
long_exit: highest((close > open) & ((high - close) < 0.2 * (close - open)) & ((open - low) >= 2 * (close - open)) & (abs(low - shift(low, 1)) <= 0.005 * close), 5) < 1
notes: Wick multiple and 'near' not quantified in the excerpt; 2x body and within 0.5% of the prior low assumed. Published as a failed filter.

name: BTC 10-day closing range <= 2.1%, hold N days
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: When BTC's 10-day closing range narrows to 2.1% or less, buying the next open produced positive average returns, with the short-term edge (7-60 days) unchanged in the last five years.
notes: Closing range measured relative to the lowest close (definition not given).

name: BTC 20-day closing range <= 4.25% above a rising 365MA
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: A tight 20-day closing range (<= 4.25%) while BTC is above a rising 365-day MA beat buy-and-hold at 60-day to 1-year holds, with much smaller worst trades.
long_exit: highest(((highest(close, 20) - lowest(close, 20)) / lowest(close, 20) <= 0.0425) & (close > sma(close, 365)) & (sma(close, 365) > shift(sma(close, 365), 1)), n) < 1
notes: Sample size not stated.

name: Short BTC the day before CME expiration
author: Quantpedia
summary: In the 2017-2024 sample BTC returns were negative on the day before the last-Friday CME futures expiration (d-1), ahead of a strong expiry day.
notes: Signal at the Wednesday close before the last Friday; short the Thursday. Pattern reportedly reversed after the BITO launch (Oct 2021).

name: Hold BTC from halving to the projected cycle top
author: REKTelligence Report
summary: Past cycle highs came 367, 526 and 338/548 days after halvings; hold from the halving until the matching day count.
notes: Article gives projected dates, not a trading rule, and suggests confirming with Pi Cycle/MVRV (not expressible). Unlike cal-halving-clock-quantpedia, no re-entry at the bear-market bottom.
